title: Game-Guided Skill Discovery through Self-Play for Playable Agent Control
abstract: arXiv:2609.40137v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We present Game-Guided Skill Discovery (GGSD), a framework that uses self-play in games to discover motor skills that are directly playable by humans. Playable skills provide a compact abstraction for controlling embodied agents through a small set of learned behaviors rather than low-level actions. To be effective, these skills should be semantically distinct, interpretable, and expressive; properties that existing unsupervised skill-discovery methods often fail to achieve simultaneously. GGSD achieves these desiderata by grounding skill discovery in competitive gameplay. A hierarchical agent competes against its past selves, with a high-level policy selecting from a small discrete skill set and a skill-conditioned low-level policy learning the corresponding behaviors. translated_title: 基于游戏自对弈的技能发现用于可玩的智能体控制
translated_abstract: 我们提出了游戏引导技能发现框架，该框架利用游戏中的自对弈来发现人类可以直接操控的运动技能。可玩技能通过一小组学习到的行为而非低层动作，为控制具身智能体提供了紧凑的抽象。为了发挥作用，这些技能应当在语义上彼此不同、可解释且富有表现力——而现有的无监督技能发现方法往往无法同时实现这些特性。GGSD通过将技能发现植根于对抗性的游戏对局中来实现这些目标：一个分层的智能体与其过去的自我进行对抗，其中高层策略从一小组离散技能中进行选择，而技能条件化的低层策略学习相应的行为。训练完成后，人类可以替代高层策略，通过相同的离散技能直接控制智能体。尽管高层动作数量很少……
tldr: GGSD通过让智能体在游戏中与过去的自我进行自对弈对抗，发现了语义可区分、可解释且富有表现力的技能，训练后人类可以直接使用相同的离散技能来操控智能体。
en_tdlr: GGSD discovers semantically distinct, interpretable, and expressive skills by having hierarchical agents self-play against their past selves in games, enabling humans to directly control agents through the same small set of discrete skills after training.
